issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a method addGuestStudents(int, String) that accepts a number of new guest students and a reason, but the solution implements addGuestStudents(int) with only one parameter. This parameter mismatch (missing String reason) conflicts with the specified API and will confuse students and/or break tests that expect the two-parameter signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the implementation in the solution (and provide the same signature in the template) to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) and update the method body to add numberOfNewGuestStudents to numberOfGuestStudents. Optionally record or log the reason if desired. Ensure the template's TODO and any tests align with this two-parameter signature.

issues.description: The problem statement (and UML) require a method addGuestStudents(int, String) that accepts a number of new guest students and a reason string, but the solution implementation defines addGuestStudents(int) with only the integer parameter. The template contains a TODO for this method but no signature. This signature mismatch between the intended API (problem/UML) and the provided solution can confuse students about the expected method signature and how to implement or call it.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signature across artifacts. Either update the solution to implement public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) (and handle or log the reason), or change the problem/UML to require only addGuestStudents(int). The recommended fix is to add the String reason parameter to the solution method signature so it matches the problem statement and UML.
